tags: why do dogs circle before lying down
script: Watch your dog before they lie down and you'll almost always see the same thing, a few quick spins before they finally flop. This ritual is ancient, tracing back to wild ancestors who circled tall grass to flatten it into a comfortable, safe sleeping spot and to check the area for anything dangerous hiding nearby. It also helped them figure out wind direction so they could sleep facing the best position to catch a scent of approaching predators. Your dog doesn't need to do any of that on a soft dog bed, but the instinct never left their DNA. So that little pre-nap spin isn't quirky, it's a survival ritual thousands of years in the making.
